Top 4 qualify for the playoffs
The winner of QF 1 qualifies directly to the finals; the loser moves to QF 2
The 3rd and 4th placed teams feature in the Eliminator; the winner qualifes for QF 2; the loser is eliminated

A total of 74 matches with each franchise playing 14 games in a home and away fashion (7 games each)
Teams are grouped in a set of seven each according to previous performances and rankings
With the total number of matches being capped at 74, all teams don't play each other twice
A team plays 5 of its opponents twice while they face the remaining 4 opponents once in every cycle
A team can play its home matches at one designated venue or multiple venues
Each team is allowed to use a designated impact player at any stage of the game
The impact player should be amongst the 5 players named in the playing sheet
The named impact player usually replaces another player who has already batted / bowled
Impact players are also used in terms of tactics / collapses (batting / bowling)
The player who has been replaced will play no further role in the match
In case of an overseas impact player, the said player can only feature if the team has announced 3 or less overseas players in their first XI
A maximum of 8 overseas players can be bought during the auctions
A maximum of 4 overseas players can feature in a match
In the event of an impact sub, an overseas player can be used only if 3 or less players have beeen named in the original playing XI
At no time, more than 4 overseas players can be on the field (including substitutes)
The match is declared as a tie in the case of both teams finishing with the same score at the end of the match
The result of the match is then determined through a super over
The team that batted second during the regulation time will get to bat first
Both teams nominate three batters each and a bowler for the super over
The innings is considered closed after one over / in the event of the batting team losing two wickets
In the case of scores being level, the two teams get to play another super over with the playing conditions reversed
The dismissed batters of the previous super over and the bowler used cannot be repeated under any conditions
The super overs continue until a result is obtained / the match goes past the scheduled close
In the case of time elapsement, the match ends in a tie and both teams get 1 point each
In the event of two or more teams having the same number of points at the end of the league phase
a) The first differentiator is the number of wins
b) In case of equal number of wins, the NRR comes into play and the team with a better NRR is placed higher
c) In the case of an equal NRR, the team with the better bowling strike-rate will get a higher placing
d) In case of a tie, the positions are decided on a random draw
